newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to sell military plants next year.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to sell military plants next year.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to offer for privatisation some 80 military plants next year subject to parliament's approval to raise cash for the crumbling economy, Industry Minister Lyubomir Dachev said on Thursday.
"The cabinet plans to offer parliament for approval to lift a sell-off moratorium for most military plants and retain the ban on the biggest 24 arms plants," Dachev told a news conference.
Arms production at around 100 factories in Bulgaria includes armoured personnel carriers, machineguns, anti-tank and anti-aircraft weapons, mortars and ammunition.
More sophisticated equipment in which Bulgaria says it has monopolised trade includes radios and munitions designed to disrupt enemy communications.
The plants that would be offered for sale produce spare parts for military equipment or provide maintenance services for military vehicles and aircraft.
Cabinet is expected to finalise its decision next week and then introduce it to parliament, said Dachev.
Bulgaria's defence industry suffered a sevenfold drop in arms sales as centralised planning crumbled along with the communist regime and links between Warsaw Pact countries broke up.

Arms production and sales to leftist regimes were coordinated under the Warsaw Pact, but its demise left numerous high quality arms plants scattered in Eastern European countries competing for markets.
Dachev said that many of the arms plants had difficulties in finding markets.

Bulgaria banned sell-offs for all its military plants under a privatisation law adopted in 1992. Since then the country has been criticised by external lenders for failing to privatise most of its industry and failure to deal with lossmakers.

Of a total 1,300 enterprises under the supervision of the Industry Ministry 300 have suffered losses this year. The losses total 390 billion levs which exceeds the capital of these firms by three times.
